root_cause.text: In the vidtv TS packet writer functions, `struct null_packet_write_args` and `struct pcr_write_args` were passed by value, causing kernel stack copies of these argument structs and their uninitialized padding/MSAN metadata, which triggered uninitialized-value use warnings.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that `vidtv_ts_null_write_into()` and `vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into()` "take their argument structs by value, causing MSAN to report uninit-value warnings" and the patch changes both function signatures and callers from by-value arguments to `const ... *args` "avoiding the stack copy of the struct along with its MSAN shadow and origin metadata."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly states that `vidtv_ts_null_write_into()` and `vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into()` "take their argument structs by value, causing MSAN to report uninit-value warnings" and the patch changes both function signatures and callers from by-value arguments to `const ... *args` "avoiding the stack copy of the struct along with its MSAN shadow and origin metadata."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the PCR write call by passing a pointer to the argument structure so PCR data is written correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into() was changed to pass the address of the local variable args instead of passing args by value.
intent_record.how: This makes the function receive a pointer to the PCR write arguments structure, matching a pointer-based interface and allowing it to read or modify the populated fields correctly at runtime; passing the struct by value here would be incompatible and could prevent correct PCR packet writing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix vidtv_ts_null_write_into() invocation by passing the argument structure by pointer so null-packet padding works correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to vidtv_ts_null_write_into() inside the loop was changed from passing args by value to passing &args by pointer.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now receives the address of the args structure instead of a copy, matching a pointer-based interface so it can correctly read and possibly update the provided fields while writing null TS packets; this prevents incorrect argument passing and associated misbehavior or build failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass null packet write arguments by const pointer instead of by value to avoid unnecessary copying without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The function signature of vidtv_ts_null_write_into was changed from taking a struct null_packet_write_args by value to taking a const pointer to struct null_packet_write_args.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now receives the argument structure by reference instead of copying it on entry, avoiding a full struct copy and preventing the function from modifying the caller-provided struct through this parameter due to the const qualifier; behavior is otherwise intended to remain the same aside from calling convention and efficiency.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix vidtv_ts_null_write_into() to correctly dereference the null_packet_write_args pointer when accessing its fields.
intent_record.what: The code changes member access in vidtv_ts_null_write_into() from direct struct-style access on args to pointer-style access, replacing args.continuity_counter, args.dest_buf, args.dest_offset, and args.buf_sz with args->continuity_counter, args->dest_buf, args->dest_offset, and args->buf_sz throughout the function.
intent_record.how: This makes the function treat args as a pointer to struct null_packet_write_args rather than a struct value, allowing it to correctly dereference the passed argument structure and access its fields without invalid access or compilation errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into to take a const pointer to its argument structure instead of copying it by value.
intent_record.what: The function signature of vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into was changed from taking a struct pcr_write_args by value to taking a const pointer to struct pcr_write_args, and the field accesses inside the function were updated from dot notation to pointer dereferences for pid and continuity_counter.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now reads its input argument structure through a pointer instead of copying the whole structure on entry, while also preventing modification of the passed-in argument structure through the const qualifier. The observable behavior of constructing the TS header from the same fields remains unchanged aside from avoiding the by-value copy and requiring callers to pass an address.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into` to correctly dereference the `pcr_write_args` pointer when accessing buffer, offset, size, and PCR fields.
intent_record.what: The code updates all accesses to the function argument from struct-style field access using `args.field` to pointer-style field access using `args->field` in `vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into`, including `dest_buf`, `dest_offset`, `buf_sz`, and `pcr` across the memcpy, PCR write, and memset calls.
intent_record.how: This makes the function treat `args` as a pointer to a `struct pcr_write_args` instead of a struct value, allowing the code to compile and correctly dereference the passed argument when writing the TS header, adaptation field, PCR bits, and padding into the destination buffer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Change vidtv_ts_null_write_into to accept a const argument-structure pointer instead of a by-value struct.
intent_record.what: The function declaration for vidtv_ts_null_write_into was changed from taking a struct null_packet_write_args by value to taking a const pointer to struct null_packet_write_args.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now receives the argument structure by reference instead of copying it, avoiding a struct copy and indicating the callee must not modify the provided arguments; callers must pass an address rather than a value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Change vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into to accept a const pointer to pcr_write_args instead of a by-value struct parameter.
intent_record.what: The function declaration for vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into was changed from taking a struct pcr_write_args argument by value to taking a const struct pcr_write_args * pointer argument.
intent_record.how: At runtime this changes the function interface to receive the PCR write arguments indirectly through a read-only pointer instead of copying the whole structure on call, requiring callers to pass an address and preventing the callee from modifying the provided argument data through this parameter type.

Change vidtv_ts_pcr_write_into to accept a const pointer to pcr_write_args instead of a by-value struct parameter.
Change vidtv_ts_null_write_into to accept a const argument-structure pointer instead of a by-value struct.

This group directly changes those helper APIs to take const pointers instead of by-value structs, matching the root cause and preventing those problematic copies.

The vulnerability is caused by passing argument structs by value in vidtv TS packet writer functions, which copies uninitialized padding/metadata from the kernel stack. This change directly addresses that root cause for vidtv_ts_null_write_into by switching from a by-value struct to a const pointer.
